  "id": "FEAT-004",
  "type": "feat",
  "description": "Replace the fall-detection dashboard UI with a minimal sitting/standing web app and update the docs. User requirements: 'Make a website as well. Make it minimal and stay away from gradients or weird fonts. Stick with a pretty basic font and it should be like a dashboard showing how long you've been sitting, how long you've been standing, etc'; 'It will include a bunch of health information on the site'; data on how often people sit and stand that can be shared with health providers; the timed calibration sequence with clear instructions on when to leave, come back, walk, stand still and sit.   "status": "in_progress",
  "steps": [
    "Rewrite dashboard/static/index.html, style.css and app.js (you may split JS into a few files under dashboard/static/ if it stays CSP-compatible: no inline scripts/styles/handlers, no external URLs; check the CSP constant in dashboard/server.py). Single page with a simple top nav (hash routing): Today, History, Health, Share, Calibrate, Sensor.",
    "Visual rules: light theme, flat solid colours only (no CSS gradients anywhere, remove the radial-gradient brand mark), system font stack only (font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; no @font-face, no web fonts, no monospace display fonts except optional tabular-nums), generous whitespace, thin borders, at most one accent colour plus a distinct colour per state (sitting / standing / moving / away). Accessible: semantic headings, labels for inputs, aria-live for the current posture and calibration countdown, colour is never the only signal (text labels on charts/legend), keyboard focus visible, sufficient contrast.",
    "Today page (default): large current state ('Sitting', 'Standing', 'Moving', 'Away', 'Unknown' + reason such as 'Not calibrated - calibrate the room'), confidence, 'Sitting for 23 min' current streak, tiles for Sitting today, Standing today, Moving today, Upright total, Stand hours X / goal, Sit-to-stand transitions, Longest sitting bout; an hourly canvas bar chart (24 bars, stacked sitting vs upright minutes, with axis labels and a text legend); a stand reminder banner when the API reports an active reminder ('You have been sitting for 30 min. Time to stand up for a minute.') with Snooze 10 min, plus an optional browser Notification (ask permission only on a user click) and a short WebAudio beep. Show a clear SYNTHETIC banner whenever the source is simulation, and a 'Replay, not saved' note for replay.",
    "History page: last 7 / 30 days table and simple bar chart of daily sitting vs upright hours, average sitting bout length, transitions per day, stand hours per day (from /api/posture/history).",
    "Health page: concise, factual, non-prescriptive information about prolonged sitting, written as general information, not medical advice. Cite real sources only, as plain text references (no links required to work offline; if links are added they must not load resources): WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour (World Health Organization, 2020): adults should limit sedentary time and replace it with physical activity of any intensity; Dunstan DW et al., 'Breaking up prolonged sitting reduces postprandial glucose and insulin responses', Diabetes Care 2012;35(5):976-983. Show the user's own 7-day averages next to the information (average daily sitting time, average sitting bout, share of hours with a stand break). Include 'Talk to your healthcare provider for advice about your situation.' Do not invent statistics.",
    "Share page: explain what is collected (only time spent sitting/standing/moving/away and reminder responses, stored locally in data/posture.sqlite3, no camera, no audio, nothing sent anywhere automatically), a date range selector, buttons to download CSV and JSON from /api/posture/export, and a print-friendly provider summary (period, daily averages, bouts, transitions, stand hours, method note and disclaimer) using a @media print stylesheet and window.print() bound via addEventListener.",
    "Calibrate page: before starting, show the full planned schedule from session.timeline (GET /api/calibration/state after POST /api/calibration/start, or computed client-side from step_specs + defaults) as a table with clock offsets: e.g. 0:00 Press Start, leave the room (5 s); 0:05 Empty room recorded (21 s, stay out); 0:26 Come back in (5 s); 0:31 Walk back and forth (16 s); 0:47 Stop and stand still (3 s); 0:50 Standing still recorded (21 s); 1:11 Walk to the chair and sit (3 s); 1:14 Sitting recorded (21 s); 1:35 Done - total 1 min 35 s. Inputs for lead-in, grace, transition and step durations (validated, total updates live). A placement name input (existing placement validation). During the run: a big countdown for the current phase, the current instruction, what comes next, a progress bar for the whole run (solid fill, no gradient), and audio cues so the user outside the room knows when to return: a beep at every phase change plus speechSynthesis reading the phase cue (toggle, on by default, tested with a 'Test sound' button that also unlocks audio). Show per-step quality (ok_fraction, failures with the redo button), and when computed: posture self-check accuracy (labelled 'within-calibration check, optimistic'), warnings (e.g. sitting and standing look similar), and Save. Show the active calibration and allow Clear. Use the existing /api/calibration/* routes (start with auto=true, step/start, step/cancel, step/redo, cancel, save, load, clear).",
    "Sensor page: data source controls (serial port picker with 'auto', replay file, simulation scenario incl. desk_day, Stop) using existing /api/ports, /api/replay_files, /api/source, /api/stop; connection status (packets/s, RSSI, data quality, sensor config) from /api/status; a small live motion score chart from /api/series.     "Update tests/test_dashboard.py UI tests (e.g. test_index_serves_html_with_disclaimer, test_ui_has_alert_simulation_and_export_controls) to the new page: assert the disclaimer, nav sections, calibrate/share/health sections and element ids the JS uses; add a test that no static asset contains 'gradient' or '@font-face' or external URLs.",

## Yes, it's all done. You can calibrate and test now.

FEAT-004, the last feature, is finished. The old fall-detection page is gone, and the web app is now the minimal sitting/standing tracker. It has six pages: Today, History, Health, Share, Calibrate and Sensor. `make test` passes, and the build and JS syntax checks pass. No backend changes were needed. Nothing has been checked in a real browser or on the boards yet, so the sound, speech and layout still need your look.

**To calibrate on the real hardware:**
```bash
make dashboard ARGS="--serial /dev/cu.usbmodem2101"
```
1. Open the **Calibrate** page and enter a room name.
2. Press **Test sound**. Browsers block audio until you click once, and this click unlocks it.
3. Press **Start calibration**. It runs by itself, with a beep and a spoken instruction at every phase.

The schedule, as the backend computes it (each recorded step includes 1 s that gets thrown away):

| At | What to do | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00 | Press Start, leave the room | 5 s |
| 0:05 | Empty room recorded (stay out) | 21 s |
| 0:26 | Come back in | 5 s |
| 0:31 | Walk back and forth | 16 s |
| 0:47 | Stop walking and stand still | 3 s |
| 0:50 | Standing still recorded | 21 s |
| 1:11 | Sit down on your chair | 3 s |
| 1:14 | Sitting recorded | 21 s |
| 1:35 | Done (total 1 min 35 s) | |

4. When it finishes, press **Save**. The **Today** page should then show Sitting or Standing instead of "Not calibrated".

Yes, it's done and you can calibrate and test now. Nothing I found blocks that, so the verdict is APPROVED. It has only been run on simulated data so far; the sandbox can't open serial ports, so the real sensor path hasn't been tried.

What I checked:
- **Tests:** `make test` passes (2 skipped) and `node --check dashboard/static/app.js` passes.
- **Schedule:** the default plan matches what was asked: 0:00 leave (5 s), 0:05 empty room recorded (21 s), 0:26 come back in (5 s), 0:31 walk (16 s), 0:47 stand still transition (3 s), 0:50 standing recorded (21 s), 1:11 sit transition (3 s), 1:14 sitting recorded (21 s), 1:35 total. Each recorded step is 1 s longer than its setting because the first second is thrown away while the signal settles.
- **Short test run:** I ran a shortened calibration over the HTTP API on the `desk_day` simulation. All four steps recorded at the expected times, the result was computed and saved as a synthetic calibration, and `/api/posture` then reported a calibrated "standing".
- **UI:** it beeps and speaks a cue at each phase, including while you're on another page. The Today page shows the live state and turns it to "unknown" when data is more than 5 s old. There are no gradients, only system fonts, no medical claims, and simulated data is labelled and never saved.

How to test with the real boards: connect the receiver on the Sensor page, open Calibrate, press Start, and follow the spoken cues. Press "Test sound" first so you know you'll hear "Come back in" from outside the room.

Three issues, none blocking:
1. **Fidgeting while seated may count as standing (likely).** The movement threshold is set without looking at the sitting step. Typing or shifting in the chair can become "moving" after 1 s, and moving counts as upright. Watch the Sensor page's motion chart during your first real session; if upright time looks too high, this is the likely cause.
2. **Calibration gets written into your history (confirmed, minor).** The ~95 s of walking, standing and sitting during a real-sensor calibration is saved to `posture.sqlite3` as real activity. The fix is to pause tracking while a calibration is running.
3. **Schedule table is hidden during the run (confirmed, cosmetic).** The countdown, next step and "time left of 1 min 35 s" still show; only the per-phase list disappears. A spoken cue can also be cut off by the next one during the 3 s position changes, but the beep still marks the change.

The review is in `.agents/tasks/task-sitting-standing-tracker/2026-10-24-183052-review.md`.

# Hands-free room calibration and sitting/standing tracker (v1)

EchoGuard moves from fall detection to a sitting/standing time tracker. One Start click runs a hands-free calibration on a timed schedule: leave the room, empty room recorded, come back in, walk, stand still, sit. The UI beeps and speaks at every phase. The recorded per-subcarrier amplitude profiles train a per-room diagonal-Gaussian sitting/standing/empty model. A live classifier with hysteresis feeds a tracker that records bouts, sitting streaks, stand reminders and stand hours. ## High-level view

The calibration timeline is computed once on the server (`build_timeline`), fixed when Start is pressed, and mirrored in JS for the pre-run plan. Waits (lead-in, grace, transition) run on the wall clock. Recorded steps run on packet time, and each step drops its first `settle_s` (= `window_s`, 1 s) so the analysis window clears. That is why each 20 s step shows as 21 s. A failed step stops the run and leaves a "Continue" path that resumes from the failed step with a "Get ready" lead-in.

The posture model selects the 16 subcarriers with the best sitting-vs-standing Fisher score. It is checked with a temporal half-split self-check that the code and UI label as optimistic and not validated. When separation is weak, the result carries a placement warning instead of failing. When the model cannot be fitted, the calibration still saves with thresholds only, and the Today page says to recalibrate. The live classifier never reports sitting or standing without a model.

Live state reaches the Today page through `/api/posture`, polled every 2 s; readings older than 5 s turn into "unknown". The UI is system-font, gradient-free and makes no network calls. The health page makes no medical claims. Synthetic and replay data get banners and are never saved.

2. **Calibration run pollutes history** (confirmed, minor) — `PostureService` keeps tracking and persisting during a live calibration, so the 95 s of walking/standing/sitting goes into `posture.sqlite3`. Skip tracker updates while `CalibrationManager.session.running`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Timed run state machine

```
Start ─▶ lead_in 5s (wall) ─▶ empty_baseline 1+20s (packet) ─▶ grace 5s ─▶ walking 1+15s
      ─▶ transition 3s ─▶ standing_still 1+20s ─▶ transition 3s ─▶ sitting 1+20s ─▶ compute
```

`CalibrationSession` only moves forward on engine frames or on `state()` polls. A waiting phase therefore depends on the UI's 500 ms poll, which runs on every page while a run is active. Each new cue calls `speechSynthesis.cancel()` before speaking. The 3 s transition cue ("Stop walking and stand still. Recording starts in 3 seconds.") takes about as long to say as the transition lasts, so the next cue can cut off its last words (likely, cosmetic). The beep still marks the boundary.

### Posture model and live classification

Training uses only quality-OK frames. At runtime `PostureClassifier` classifies only frames whose motion score is below the movement threshold, averaging a 3 s window, with a 5 s hold or a 2 s confirm after movement. That threshold is `quiet_p95 + 0.5 * (walk_median - quiet_p95)`, where `quiet_p95` uses the empty room and standing still but not sitting. The only sitting-related warning fires when the sitting median exceeds `rapid`. Someone who types or shifts in the chair more than they did during the 20 s still-sitting step goes to `moving` after 1 s (`MOVING_CONFIRM_S`). `UPRIGHT_STATES` treats moving as upright, so that time counts toward stand hours and can end a sitting streak through `stand_break_s` (likely). This doesn't block calibration or testing, but it is the most probable source of inflated upright numbers in real use. It is worth watching on the Sensor page's motion chart during the first live test.

### History during calibration

`PostureService._on_frame` runs for every frame whatever the calibration state is. During a live calibration the user walks, stands and sits for about 95 s. Those minutes are classified under the previously active model (or as unknown/moving without one) and saved to `posture.sqlite3` as real bouts (confirmed). This is minor for a single test session, but it accumulates if the user recalibrates often.

### Dashboard calibration page

During a run, `renderRun` keeps calling `renderPlanTable` with the current index, but the table is inside the hidden `cal-setup` card. The run card's progress text still shows the time left out of 1 min 35 s, so the total is visible but the per-phase list is not (confirmed, cosmetic).
